summary: token-bucket sync failure causes pinned-model fallback during canary rollout
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary rollout for redwood-v2-quant (tenant-scoped rollout for Clipr Labs, dedicated tier), a subset of requests that had active model pins were being routed to the fallback model variant. Customers reported sudden quality regressions and mixed outputs for pinned sessions.

Impact:
- ~1.8% of Clipr Labs traffic in us-east was served by the fallback model for pinned sessions over a 27-minute window.
- Customer-visible quality regressions for chat completions and hallucination rate increase reported.
- No broader platform-wide alert; localized to us-east edge cluster dealing with canary cohort.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (edge cluster: edge-us-east-3)
- Customer: Clipr Labs (dedicated capacity pool assigned)
- Rollout: weighted canary 5% -> 10% in progress at time of incident

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Simulate tenant with pinned sessions sending steady request rate through edge-us-east-3.
2) Introduced canary traffic by marking subset of hosts as v2-canary and starting rollout.
3) Several edge proxies returned 429/over-quota responses then the routing layer invoked fallback policy even when a model pin existed.
4) After fallback, session responses came from redwood-v2-legacy variant (fallback model) instead of pinned v2-quant.

Observed logs/snippets:
- edge-proxy logs: "token-bucket: local-balance=0, tenant=clipr-123, decision=reject -> fallback-route"
- rate-limiter ec2 metrics: token-sync lag spikes at 03:12:14 UTC; hop-count mismatch between proxies: 3 vs 1.
- routing trace: "pin=yes but local-throttle=true => applied fallback policy"

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent change to token-bucket synchronization (PR referenced below) introduced an infrequent race where bucket-sync daemon fell behind for newly-promoted canary hosts. Proxies with stale token balance interpreted tenant as over-quota and invoked fallback-circuit despite pinned routing decisions. Because local throttle check ran before pin-coherence check in the routing path, fallback took precedence.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed correlation between token-sync lag and fallback events using tracing (trace IDs attached in comments).
- Replayed traffic against a reproduce cluster with intentional bucket-sync lag; observed deterministic fallback behavior when sync lag > 12s.
- Audit of deployment shows edge-proxy config was updated 2026-03-10 02:50 UTC to change token-bucket sync interval from 5s -> 30s (to reduce DB load) in canary hosts only (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/462).
- Routing path analysis shows ordering: local-throttle check -> pin-check -> route decision. When local-throttle rejects, routing code sets fallback even if pin-check would prefer original model. This ordering predates recent rollout logic.

Customer communication summary:
- 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC: initial alert from Clipr Labs support contact (noise of mixed-quality responses).
- 2026-03-10 03:55 UTC: Support acknowledged, escalated to SRE and serving-runtime.
- 2026-03-10 04:12 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied and communicated to customer.

Mitigation and resolution:
- Immediate mitigation (03:57 UTC): increased local token balance on affected proxies and forced token-sync to run ad-hoc across cluster (manual kick). This restored normal routing for pinned sessions within ~8 minutes.
- Code rollback (04:05 UTC): reverted canary-specific token-sync interval change so all hosts use 5s sync.
- Hotfix (deployed 2026-03-10 10:30 UTC): added routing guard so model-pin check has priority over local throttle for pinned sessions; local-throttle re-evaluated as a soft-fail (logs counters) rather than immediate fallback for pinned sessions.
- Post-deploy verification: 12:00 UTC automated checks confirmed no pinned-session fallbacks for 24h window; Clipr Labs verified quality restored.

Root cause:
1) Token-bucket sync interval change on canary hosts created out-of-sync local balances.
2) Routing logic evaluated local-throttle before honoring model-pin, causing premature fallback decisions when local-balance was stale.

Follow-up actions (owners):
- edge-proxy (Marcus Reed): strengthen token-sync telemetry and add alert for token-sync lag > 5s (ETA 2026-03-15).
- routing (Lena Zhang): make pin-check highest-priority decision in routing path and add unit/integration tests (ETA 2026-03-18).
- release (Infra Eng): revert any environment-specific throttling config changes without compatibility checks for pin semantics (process update, ETA 2026-03-16).
- SRE (Diego Morales): run a targeted chaos test simulating token-sync lag to validate no pinned fallbacks (ETA 2026-03-20).

Attachments and references:
- Slack thread: #support-clipr (slack.com/archives/C03XXXXX)
- Traces: trace IDs: 6a4f2b9c, b7e3f8d1 (available in tracing UI)
- GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/462
- Confluence: confluence.internal/redwood/canary-rollout-runbook

Resolution notes:
- Incident declared resolved after hotfix and verification. Root-cause actions scheduled and tracked. Customer credited 2 days of Dedicated support as goodwill; finance notified.

Postmortem required: yes (owner: Diego Morales).
